mainTopic: Marking places of corpse טומאה (צִיּוּן): which remains and doubtful places are marked, and the kinds of בית הפרס
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story from the previous page with a פסוק that רבי ינאי applied to his student. Then a ברייתא teaches the rules of marking places of corpse טומאה with a צִיּוּן: which remains are marked, that only doubtful places are marked, and that the marker goes near the spot, not on it and not far away. The גמרא asks how a כזית of a corpse can go unmarked when a משנה says it makes things טמא through an אהל. רב פפא answers that an exact כזית will soon shrink, so a marker would mislead people forever. The גמרא then defines the doubtful places: overhanging branches, protruding stones, and a בית הפרס. When it challenges whether a בית הפרס really makes things טמא through an אהל, רב פפא splits it into two kinds: a field where a grave was lost and a field where a grave was plowed. A משנה lists three kinds of בית הפרס, and the גמרא explains the third, the weepers' field. Finally, a ברייתא about a marked field with trees is answered: the field was marked for a lost grave that was later plowed, and the trees stand along the borders.

steps.title: Closing the story with a verse from תהלים
steps.stepSummary: The previous story ends with רבי ינאי applying the פסוק 'ושם דרך אראנו בישע אלהים' to his student.
steps.simpleTranslation: He read this verse about him: 'And to him who orders his way, I will show the salvation of God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a story that began on the previous page. It ends with a פסוק that praises the person in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person in the story weighed his conduct carefully and knew when it was not proper to challenge his teacher. The פסוק is read as praise for someone who 'sets his way', meaning he thinks before he acts. This line closes the story, and the next step begins a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: He read (applied) a verse about him
And one who sets (plans out) his way
The salvation of God

phrases.english: He read about him:
phrases.notes: This finishes a story from the previous page: רבי ינאי reads this פסוק about his student.

phrases.english: "And to him who orders his way, I will show the salvation of God."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story carried over from the previous page
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The person who knew when not to challenge his teacher is praised with the פסוק 'ושם דרך'.

steps.title: Which human remains get a warning marker
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a כזית of a corpse, a bone the size of a barley grain, and anything that does not make things טמא through an אהל are not marked. The spine, the skull, and most of the skeleton (by structure or by count of bones) are marked.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We do not mark an olive-size of a corpse, nor a bone the size of a barley grain, nor anything that does not make things טמא through a tent. But we do mark the spine, the skull, the majority of the body's frame, and the majority of the number of the corpse's bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about putting up a צִיּוּן (warning marker) over corpse טומאה. This first part says which remains get a marker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sorts remains into two groups. Small pieces are not marked: a כזית of flesh, a barley-size bone, and anything that does not spread טומאה through an אהל. Large, significant remains are marked: the spine, the skull, רוב בנין (most of the body's frame), and רוב מנין (most of the bones by count).

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
We mark (put up a warning sign over טומאה)
An olive-size piece of a corpse
Makes things טמא by being under the same roof or overhang
Most of the body's frame (the large bones)
Most of the bones by number

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'nor anything that does not make things טמא through a tent' makes it sound as if the כזית and the barley-size bone listed before it are also things that don't spread טומאה through an אהל. That reading is exactly what the גמרא will challenge in step 4.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the starting point for the whole discussion that follows about why some real sources of טומאה are still not marked.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְצַיְּנִין לֹא עַל כַּזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת,
phrases.english: We do not mark an olive-size of a corpse,
phrases.notes: 'Marking' means putting up a warning sign so people carrying pure items know to stay away.

phrases.english: nor a bone the size of a barley grain,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא בְּאֹהֶל.
phrases.english: nor anything that does not make things impure through a tent.
But we do mark the spine,
and the skull,
the majority of the frame,
and the majority of the number of the corpse's bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְצַיְּנִין לֹא עַל כַּזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic unrelated to the closing story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small remains (a כזית, a barley-size bone, anything that does not make things טמא through an אהל) are not marked. The spine, the skull, רוב בנין and רוב מנין are marked.

steps.title: Mark doubtful places, and place the marker carefully
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: places of certain טומאה are not marked, but places of doubtful טומאה (overhanging branches, protrusions, a בית הפרס) are. The marker goes neither right on the spot nor far from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not mark places of certain impurity, but we do mark places of doubtful impurity. These are the doubtful places: overhanging branches, protrusions, and a בית הפרס. We do not put the marker right on the place of impurity, so as not to ruin pure items. And we do not put the marker far from the place of impurity, so as not to lose land of ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא keeps going. It says which places are marked (doubtful ones) and gives two rules about exactly where to put the marker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A place known for certain to be טמא needs no marker because everyone already knows about it. A place of ספק טומאה does need one, because people would not know. The marker must sit a little before the spot: if it were right on the spot, a person carrying טהרות would already be there before seeing it. If it were far away, a large area would needlessly be treated as off-limits.

keyTerms.meaning: Places of certain impurity
Places of doubtful impurity
Overhanging branches and protruding stones or ledges
An area where a grave was plowed up and bones may be scattered
Ritually pure food and items

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's rules: small remains are not marked, while the spine, the skull and most of the body are. Doubtful places are marked, and certain ones are not. The marker goes near the spot, not on it and not far away.

phrases.english: And we do not mark places of certain impurity,
but we do mark places of doubtful impurity.
And these are the doubtful places:
overhanging branches, protrusions, and a בית הפרס.
And we do not set up the marker on the place of impurity,
so as not to ruin the pure items.
phrases.notes: By the time someone saw a marker sitting right on the spot, their pure food would already be טמא.

phrases.english: And we do not distance the marker from the place of impurity,
so as not to cause a loss of ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מְצַיְּנִין עַל הַוַּודָּאוֹת, אֲבָל מְצַיְּנִין עַל הַסְּפֵיקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with more rules
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only doubtful places of טומאה are marked, and the marker is placed close to the spot, not on it and not far from it.

steps.title: Doesn't a כזית of a corpse make things טמא through a tent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: it seemed to say a כזית of a corpse does not make things טמא through an אהל, but a משנה lists a כזית of a corpse among the things that do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does an olive-size of a corpse really not make things impure through a tent? But we learned in a משנה: 'These make things impure through a tent: an olive-size of a corpse!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins analyzing the ברייתא by raising a contradiction from a משנה in מסכת אהלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed 'a כזית of a corpse' next to 'anything that does not make things טמא through a tent'. That makes it sound like a כזית is in that weaker group. But the משנה clearly says a כזית of a corpse does make things טמא through an אהל, so the גמרא asks how the ברייתא can mean that.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a contradicting source)
These are the things that make things טמא through a tent

phrases.english: And an olive-size of a corpse
does not make things impure through a tent?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
These are the things that make things impure through a tent:
an olive-size of a corpse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the ברייתא quoted in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's grouping of a כזית of a corpse with 'anything that does not make things טמא through an אהל'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies a כזית does not make things טמא through an אהל. A משנה in אהלות explicitly says it does, so the two sources seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: An exact כזית will shrink, so it is not marked
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the ברייתא is talking about a piece of flesh that is exactly a כזית. It will soon decay to less than a כזית. So it is better not to mark it. Then only a little תרומה and קדשים might be burned now, instead of being burned forever because of a marker that is no longer true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here we are talking about a piece that is exactly a כזית. In the end it will shrink. It is better that תרומה and קדשים be burned because of it for a short time, and not be burned because of it forever.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from step 4. A כזית does make things טמא through an אהל, but the ברייתא is not marking it for a practical reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never meant that a כזית of a corpse does not make things טמא through an אהל. The piece in our case is exactly a כזית, so it will soon decay and stop giving off טומאה. If it were marked, people would keep treating the spot as טמא and burning their תרומה and קדשים long after the טומאה was gone. Not marking it causes only a short-term loss.

keyTerms.meaning: exactly the size of an olive, not even a little more
it will surely shrink
it is better
the portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be burned if it becomes טמא
holy things, such as קרבנות
for the time being, temporarily

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא is saying a כזית of a corpse is not טמא. It is fully טמא and makes things טמא through an אהל. The only question is whether to put up a marker, and the answer is no because the piece will soon shrink.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that marking a grave is a practical safety step. חז״ל weigh a short-term risk against a misleading sign that would cause loss for years.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Here we are dealing with exactly an olive-size piece,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the ברייתא from step 2, which said a כזית is not marked.

phrases.english: which in the end will certainly shrink.
It is better that there be burned because of it
תרומה and holy things for the time being,
phrases.notes: If someone walks over the unmarked spot now, he becomes טמא, and his תרומה or קדשים must be burned.

phrases.english: and not be burned because of it forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָכָא בִּכְזַיִת מְצוּמְצָם עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 4 by narrowing which case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is talking about a piece that is exactly a כזית.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that a כזית of a corpse does not make things טמא through an אהל, which would contradict the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כזית does make things טמא through an אהל. An exact כזית is not marked only because it will soon shrink, and a marker would then mislead people forever.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An exact כזית of a corpse is not marked, because a temporary loss is better than a permanent one.

steps.title: Explaining the doubtful places: overhanging branches and protruding stones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's list of places where there is a doubt about טומאה, the places that do get marked. It explains two of them. סככות are tree branches hanging over the ground. פרעות are stones sticking out of a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the doubtful places: overhanging branches and protrusions. Overhanging branches are a tree that hangs over the ground. Protrusions are stones that stick out from a wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first quotes the ברייתא's words again to set up its explanation. Then it defines the two unclear terms, סככות and פרעות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the doubtful places that step 3 said do get marked. In each one, a branch or a stone covers some ground, and a corpse might be lying underneath. If one is, the covering acts as an אהל and makes anyone who passes under it טמא. Since no one knows for sure, a marker warns people to stay away.

keyTerms.meaning: doubtful cases, places where we are not sure if there is טומאה
overhanging branches
stones sticking out of a wall
hangs over and covers
a fence or wall

steps.whatToRemember: An exact כזית is not marked because it will soon shrink. Doubtful places, like branches or stones that might cover a corpse, are marked so people know to avoid them.

phrases.english: And these are the doubtful places:
overhanging branches and protrusions.
Overhanging branches —
a tree that hangs over the ground.
Protrusions —
protruding stones
that stick out from the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the question about the כזית, the גמרא returns to the next part of the ברייתא and explains its terms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סככות are tree branches over the ground, and פרעות are stones sticking out of a wall. Both are doubtful places that might cover a corpse, so they are marked.

steps.title: Defining a בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the third doubtful place from the ברייתא. A בית הפרס is a field where someone plowed over a grave, and the area covers one hundred אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a בית הפרס? As a משנה teaches: someone who plows over a grave turns that area into a בית הפרס. How big an area does he make into a בית הפרס? The full length of a furrow, which is one hundred אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues defining the words from the ברייתא's list of doubtful places. Now it explains the last one, בית הפרס, by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a plow passes over a grave, it may drag small bones across the field. Because we do not know where those bones ended up, the field becomes a place of doubtful טומאה. The משנה sets the size of that area at one full furrow, one hundred אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed, so bones may be scattered around it
As we learned in a משנה
One who plows
A furrow, the length a plow goes before turning
A cubit, a measure of length

phrases.english: A beit haperas is as we learned in a mishna:
One who plows over a grave
turns it into a beit haperas.
And how much area does he turn into one?
The full length of a furrow, which is a hundred cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of definitions started in step 6 by explaining the third doubtful place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plowing over a grave makes a בית הפרס that covers one hundred אמות.

steps.title: Does a בית הפרס really make things טמא through an אהל?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's rule implied that a בית הפרס makes things טמא through an אהל, because only such places get marked. The גמרא challenges this with two אמוראים who treat a בית הפרס leniently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a בית הפרס really make things טמא through an אהל? But רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a person may blow on the ground of a בית הפרס and keep walking. And רב יהודה בר אמי said in the name of עולא: a בית הפרס that has been trampled is טהור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that a בית הפרס makes things טמא through an אהל. It brings two rulings that treat a בית הפרס much more leniently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that whatever does not make things טמא through an אהל is not marked, yet it said a בית הפרס is marked. So a בית הפרס must make things טמא through an אהל. But שמואל lets a person blow bones out of his path and walk on, and עולא says a well-trodden field is טהור. Both rulings only work if a bone can make you טמא only by touching it, not through an אהל.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes things טמא by being under the same roof or overhang, without touching
Blows, to clear small bones from his path
That was trampled by many people walking through
Pure, not טמא

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says outright that a בית הפרס makes things טמא through an אהל. The גמרא is putting two parts of it together: only such places are marked, and a בית הפרס is marked.

phrases.english: But does a beit haperas really make things impure through a tent?
But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Shmuel said:
A person may blow on the ground of a beit haperas and keep walking.
phrases.notes: He blows away any small bones before each step so he will not touch them. If leaning over a bone made him טמא, blowing would not help.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda bar Ami said in the name of Ulla:
A beit haperas that has been trampled is pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הַפְּרָס מִי מְטַמֵּא בְּאֹהֶל? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that בית הפרס has been defined, the גמרא questions how it fits the ברייתא's rule about marking.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's implied claim that a בית הפרס makes things טמא through an אהל, since it is marked.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל allows blowing bones away and walking on, and עולא calls a trampled בית הפרס טהור. Both show that a בית הפרס only makes things טמא by touching, not through an אהל.

steps.title: רב פפא: two different kinds of בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that there are two kinds of בית הפרס. A field where a grave was lost makes things טמא through an אהל and is marked. A field where a grave was plowed is the lenient kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is not a problem. Here, the ברייתא is talking about a field where a grave was lost. There, שמואל and עולא are talking about a field where a grave was plowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by saying the sources are talking about two different kinds of fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a field where a grave was lost, we know a whole grave is in there somewhere, so it is strict: it makes things טמא through an אהל and gets marked. In a field where a grave was plowed, there may only be a few scattered bones, or none at all. That is why blowing them away, or a field that has been trampled, is enough to keep it טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem; the two sources do not contradict
In which a grave was lost; it is there, but its exact spot is forgotten
In which a grave was plowed, so bones may be scattered

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of בית הפרס. A field with a lost grave makes things טמא through an אהל and is marked. A field with a plowed grave is more lenient: you can blow away the bones, and if it is trampled it is טהור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains which doubtful fields need a marker, and why some fields can be crossed safely while others cannot.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is not difficult.
Here, it is a field in which a grave was lost.
phrases.notes: This first "here" is the ברייתא, which marks the field.

phrases.english: There, it is a field in which a grave was plowed.
phrases.notes: This "there" is the rulings of שמואל and עולא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּשָׂדֶה שֶׁאָבַד בָּהּ קֶבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by splitting the sources into two different cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is talking about a different kind of בית הפרס.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought all kinds of בית הפרס follow one rule, so the ברייתא and the אמוראים seemed to contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: A field with a lost grave makes things טמא through an אהל and is marked. A field with a plowed grave does not, so the lenient rulings apply to it.

steps.title: Is a plowed-grave field called a בית הפרס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a field where a grave was plowed is really called a בית הפרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is a field where a grave was plowed called a בית הפרס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick question about רב פפא's answer. It is setting up the next step, where it will bring a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said there are two kinds of בית הפרס, and one of them is a field where a grave was plowed. The גמרא wants to check that this kind of field really has that name.

keyTerms.meaning: Was plowed
Is it called

phrases.english: And a field in which a grave was plowed,
is it called a בית הפרס?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the name used in רב פפא's answer in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a field where a grave was plowed is properly called a בית הפרס.

steps.title: Yes, a משנה lists three kinds of בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes and quotes a משנה that lists three kinds of בית הפרס, including a plowed-grave field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. We learned in a משנה: There are three kinds of בית הפרס: a field where a grave was lost, a field where a grave was plowed, and a weepers' field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes and proves it from a משנה. The משנה names three kinds of בית הפרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plowed-grave field is listed by name as a בית הפרס, so רב פפא's wording is correct. The list also adds a third kind, the שדה בוכין, which the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
And we learned in a משנה
Was lost
Weepers' field

phrases.english: Yes, and we learned in a משנה:
There are three kinds of בית הפרס:
a field in which a grave was lost,
and a field in which a grave was plowed,
and a weepers' field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 with a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the משנה lists a plowed-grave field as one of three kinds of בית הפרס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה listing three kinds of בית הפרס

steps.title: What is a weepers' field?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by שדה בוכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a weepers' field?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the third item on the list means. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two kinds are clear from their names. The name weepers' field does not tell us why the field might be טמא, so the גמרא asks.

keyTerms.meaning: What is

phrases.english: What is a weepers' field?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the third item in the משנה quoted in Step 11.

steps.title: The field where people part from the dead
steps.stepSummary: רב יהושע בר אבא, in the name of עולא, says a weepers' field is where people take leave of the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהושע בר אבא said in the name of עולא: It is a field where people take leave of the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the term. A weepers' field is the place where the people walking with a body say goodbye to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Funeral groups stopped at this field to cry and part from the dead. Because many bodies passed through it, the field is treated as a possible place of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
Take leave of, say goodbye to

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר אַבָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא אָמַר:
phrases.english: רב יהושע בר אבא said in the name of עולא:
A field where people take leave of the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שדה בוכין is the field where people part from the dead.

steps.title: Why is a weepers' field a concern?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is for treating a weepers' field as possibly טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this field would be טמא at all. No grave is there. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other two kinds of field had a real grave in them. A weepers' field only has bodies passing through it, so the גמרא wants to know the reason for the concern.

keyTerms.meaning: Reason

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the case defined in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a weepers' field is treated as possibly טמא.

steps.title: Because the owners gave up on lost pieces
steps.stepSummary: אבימי says the חכמים were concerned because the owners gave up hope on any part of the body that fell there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי said: The חכמים touched on it because of the owners' giving up hope.
steps.whatsHappening: אבימי gives the reason. A piece of a body may have fallen in the field, and its owners gave up looking for it, so it stayed there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody would come back for a lost piece, it could still be lying somewhere in the field. Because of that, the חכמים treated the whole field as possibly טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The owners giving up hope
Dealt with it, made a rule about it

steps.whatToRemember: There are three kinds of בית הפרס: a field where a grave was lost, a field where a grave was plowed, and a weepers' field. A weepers' field is a concern because pieces of bodies may have been left there.

phrases.english: אבימי said:
Because of the owners' giving up hope,
phrases.notes: The owners are the family of the dead person. They gave up on finding a piece that may have fallen off.

phrases.english: they touched on it.
phrases.notes: He means the חכמים made a rule about this field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern comes from יאוש בעלים: lost body parts were given up on and left in the field.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows a plowed-grave field is marked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: a ברייתא shows that a plowed-grave field does get a marker.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a field where a grave was plowed not need a marker? But a ברייתא teaches: If one found a marked field and does not know what kind it is: if it has trees, it is known that a grave was plowed in it. If it has no trees, it is known that a grave was lost in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב פפא's answer in Step 9 and attacks it. A ברייתא talks about a marked field that turns out to be a plowed-grave field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said only a field where a grave was lost gets a marker, and a plowed-grave field does not. The ברייתא says a marked field with trees is a plowed-grave field, so a plowed-grave field must also get a ציון. That goes against רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: A marker warning people about טומאה
But a ברייתא teaches
Marked
Its nature, what kind it is
Trees

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying that trees cause anything. The trees are only a sign that tells you which kind of field it is.

phrases.english: And a field in which a grave was plowed,
does it not need a marker?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב פפא in Step 9, who said only the lost-grave field is marked.

phrases.english: But a ברייתא teaches:
If one found a marked field
and it is not known what kind it is,
if there are trees in it,
it is known that a grave was plowed in it.
If there are no trees in it,
it is known that a grave was lost in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion on the three kinds of בית הפרס, the גמרא returns to challenge רב פפא's answer from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim in Step 9 that a field where a grave was plowed is not marked.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls a marked field with trees a plowed-grave field. So a plowed-grave field does get a ציון, against רב פפא.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's condition closes the challenging source
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא used against רב פפא ends with רבי יהודה's opinion: we do not rely on the signs unless an elder or a scholar is there, because not everyone is expert in this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: not unless there is an elder or a scholar there, because not everyone is an expert in this matter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it is using to challenge רב פפא. This last line is רבי יהודה's view inside that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה adds that the signs in a marked field count only when an expert can vouch for them. The main point of the challenge from step 16 stays the same: this ברייתא talks about marking a field where a grave was plowed. That seems to go against רב פפא, so the next step must answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: An elder; here, someone old and experienced who knows the history of the area
A Torah scholar
Experts; people who really know the matter

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא שָׁם זָקֵן אוֹ תַּלְמִיד,
phrases.english: not unless there is an elder or a scholar there,
because not everyone is an expert in this matter!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא שָׁם זָקֵן אוֹ תַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quoted ברייתא that makes up the challenge in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's position about a field where a grave was plowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא talks about marking such a field, which seems to go against what רב פפא said.

steps.title: רב פפא: the source is about a lost grave, and trees tell the difference
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the ברייתא is about a field where a grave was lost and was marked for that reason. Trees in the field show that the grave was later plowed over. No trees show that the grave was only lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: That ברייתא is about a field where a grave was lost, and they marked it. If the field has trees, we know a grave was plowed in it. If it has no trees, we know a grave was lost in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends himself. He says the ברייתא is about a different kind of field than the one he was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's field was marked because a grave was lost in it, not because of plowing, so it does not prove that a plowed-grave field gets a ציון. The trees only show what happened later: people forgot about the lost grave and plowed and planted the field. If there are no trees, the grave was simply lost and never plowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was lost; nobody knows exactly where in the field it is
Marking a place so people know it may be טמא
Was plowed (over)
Trees

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
when that one was taught,
phrases.notes: "That one" means the ברייתא just quoted against him.

phrases.english: it was about a field where a grave was lost, which they marked.
If it has trees,
it is known that a grave was plowed in it;
if it has no trees,
it is known that a grave was lost in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in steps 16-17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to a different case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about a field where a grave was plowed over.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a field where a grave was lost and marked. Trees are the sign that a grave was plowed over.

steps.title: Maybe the trees are inside and the grave is outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether trees really prove the grave was plowed over. The trees might be inside the field while the grave sits outside the planted area.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry: maybe the trees are inside and the grave is outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's sign. The trees might not tell us anything about the grave itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trees show that part of the field was worked. If the grave lies outside the area with the trees, its spot may never have been plowed. Then it would only be a lost grave, so the trees prove nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us be concerned
Inside
Outside

phrases.english: But let us worry
maybe the trees are inside
and the grave is outside?
phrases.notes: If so, the grave's spot was never plowed. It was only lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the tree sign that רב פפא gave in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that trees show a grave was plowed over
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The trees and the grave might be in different spots, so the trees don't prove the grave's spot was plowed.

steps.title: Like עולא: the trees stand along the borders
steps.stepSummary: Using a statement of עולא, the גמרא answers that the trees stand along the field's borders. So the grave must be inside the area they surround.
steps.simpleTranslation: As עולא said: it is where the trees stand along the borders. Here too, it is where they stand along the borders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry from step 19. It borrows an idea that עולא said in another place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is one where the trees line the edges of the field, next to public land. People do not bury the dead in public land, so the grave cannot be outside the trees. It must be in the area that was planted and worked, which means it was plowed over, and רב פפא's sign holds.

keyTerms.meaning: As (someone) said; brings in a statement from elsewhere
Borders; the edges of the field
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: A marked field is one where a grave was lost. Trees standing along the borders show that a grave inside was plowed over.

phrases.english: As Ulla said:
where they stand along the borders;
here too:
where they stand along the borders.
phrases.notes: The trees line the edges of the field, so the grave can't be outside them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19 and saves רב פפא's tree sign.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case more narrowly, based on a parallel statement of עולא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The trees might be inside the field while the grave lies outside them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The trees stand on the borders, so the grave is inside the area that was worked and was plowed over.
